blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: `ServiceA` protects a shared balance with `synchronized`, while `ServiceB` protects the same balance with a `ReentrantLock`. Per this page, what goes wrong?

options.text: Holding either lock does not stop code that uses the other one
options.says: The page says synchronized blocks and ReentrantLock blocks do not interoperate: holding one does not prevent the other from proceeding.

options.text: The JVM refuses to load classes that use both kinds of lock
options.says: The page describes the mix as a source of subtle bugs and reasoning complexity, which it could not be if it failed to load.

options.text: The two locks merge into one, so the calls run one at a time
options.says: The page says the two mechanisms do not interoperate, so they do not act as one lock.

questions.stem: A request counter built on `AtomicInteger` goes beyond `Integer.MAX_VALUE`. Per this page, what happens, and what is the remedy?

options.text: It throws an ArithmeticException; catch it and reset the count to zero
options.says: The page says AtomicInteger wraps at Integer.MAX_VALUE; it does not throw.

options.text: It stays at the largest value; check for that cap before each increment
options.says: The page says AtomicInteger wraps around rather than stopping at its maximum.

options.text: It wraps around silently; move the count to an AtomicLong or a LongAdder
options.says: The page says AtomicInteger wraps at Integer.MAX_VALUE, and unbounded counts should use AtomicLong or LongAdder.

concepts: AtomicInteger wraps around at Integer.MAX_VALUE, so an unbounded count needs AtomicLong or LongAdder.
Mixed synchronization mechanisms do not interoperate: holding a synchronized monitor does not stop code guarded by a ReentrantLock.
